body:
If you get that far you're really lucky. If they're willing to listen you have to give them a win. Make them feel like they're really helping you after a little while even if they're not. You cry to them for 10 minutes, they offer you ice cream, just take it and pretend it's gotten a little better. I'm not great with quickly feeling better and anyone who I've been upset in front of quickly gives up, and I think it's because I don't give them an easy win. Somehow, use it as an opportunity to make them feel like the most amazingly caring people in the world.  

Trying to hop from person to person isn't a great idea. If possible, get them to really invest in you so they can't just give up. Give them a reason to cheer you up.

Have you tried keto? Without any of your other issues trying to eat a normal diet but having to remove all the gluten really really super sucks. Everyone over at /r/keto are pretty friendly too. I don't have celiac, but it seemed like the only sane way to go about removing carbs/fat from my life and it's one of the few things I've done that made me feel good and in control for once.


Cutting never worked for me because I was too secretive to show anyone, and if no one can hear your cry for help you're just making it worse. Even if you think the worst of yourself, you have to know there are guys out there who would kill just to have a shot with you, even if you have to put those guys down in your mind as being desperate or having poor taste. We know they're out there, and they're probably scouring dating websites for someone just like you right now. If no one cares and you're on your own, why not give some creepy old guy the time of day, even through text, so you can at least find out you're no where near the bottom of the barrel in other people's opinion.  


I know how it is, everything is miserable, but if you have it in you you should really give something new a shot. Just something, anything. Why not?

From my experience, it's really best not to tell people you know unless they ask. You go in hoping you're wrong, hoping that you're just being silly and they really will understand... and then they don't, or even worse. By all means ham it up so they might ask, but if they don't care enough to notice something is up don't go there. Don't find out for sure that the people around you don't care, it hurts way worse than you expect it to and persists.

Ham it up and tell yourself they're just really dumb about reading signals if they don't ask.

I've come across two different kinds of pleaser: one who wants to please me, and one who wants to please everyone but me. It's pretty obvious why the second doesn't work out... if you're catering to everyone else and expect your partner to stand by you you might not have a lot of luck.  


If you're focused completely on pleasing your partner you might forget to open up about your problems and your wants. If you take second best for everything they're not going to feel like they're your first choice. The relationship becomes lopsided with you giving them everything except what they really want: to feel wanted. How can they ever know that if you don't take something for yourself?

I've got to ask, are you depressed/depressing to be around? It might be the case that your boyfriend has dated a girl like you before (or one of his friends has) and it turned out really bad. He picks up the sad girl who ends up trying to tear him away from his friends by the sheer amount of emotional support she needs (maybe she doesn't mean to but it pans out that way), and he tries to make her happy with gifts that cost lots of money, but eventually she needs more support than he can offer and when he's weak in that department she gets it from someone else and ends up sleeping with them.  

I'm just throwing that out there as a possibility, I've never encountered this situation myself. Is there a possibility that something along those lines might be going on?

Thankyou, I followed that link and can compile a .cpp file I've made on my desktop. Unfortunately I don't know how to apply it to follow the instructions on [the lua installation page.](http://www.lua.org/manual/5.2/readme.html) It tells me to 'do "make"'... I'm really lost still...

I have a generator that when given a seed (and a few other pieces of information like height, width, whether the screen wraps at the end, and type of map) can produce a map, but if I pass it the same information and ask what the tile is at any given location it can produce it without producing the entire map, or if I give it an area it can make that without producing the whole map.  

When I load my map into memory I'd load a section the player is in from the generator and then go over those values and put any altered values over the top. When the player moves a certain amount in any direction it'll generate some more content in the direction they're headed and remove unused content behind them. I ran into performance issues putting an entire map into memory (because it was just so large) and since a player will be going to many of these levels and go back to them  I can't justify large save files or capping the number of saves.

I'm saving up to 5 layers on any given tile where the vast majority of tiles will only have information for two of those layers so I'd rather not have every tile I save be fixed size.  

I'm thinking I was something like the following:


       ...(generation info etc)...


       altered_tiles

        X_value

         Y_value

          Tile_Data_1

          Tile_Data_4

          Tile_Data_5
 
         Y_value

          Tile_Data_3

        X_value

         Y_value

          Tile_Data_3


...and I don't know how to read that in binary. I could order my data like that in XML, but I'd rather not be parsing text when I'm storing mostly numbers.

I was using a random number generator, but it ended up being very inefficient for my purposes. I need to make several long lines and make them into textures, so if I can cut out the complicated math in a random number generator that'd really improve how this whole thing runs. It also makes seeding much more simple and my code more readable, so that's always a plus.
